title: Trace-anchor bridge for multi-tenant structured log derivation
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Create a lightweight 'trace-anchor bridge' service that normalizes and forwards structured logs from edge/sidecar producers into our Loki ingestion pipeline while reliably attaching OTel trace identifiers and tenant context. The bridge's goals are: 1) preserve end-to-end correlation across async queues and batching layers; 2) emit Loki-compatible label sets without exploding cardinality; 3) apply stable tenant-safe ID translation and sampling hints for downstream metrics and dashboards.
background: We continue to see gaps linking traces to log snippets for high-latency tail investigations. Existing sidecars and firehose producers emit JSON logs but often drop or rename trace/span IDs, and tenant metadata is inconsistent across sources. Several prior efforts (ENG-41208 deterministic correlation id stitching; ENG-9054 unified-log-enrichment orchestrator) addressed pieces, but we need a small, opinionated transform/router that sits between producers and Loki/ELK to make logs reliably queryable for trace joins and SLO analysis.
scope: Implement a stateless bridge with the following functionality: 1) ingest JSON/JSONL from sidecars or Kafka; 2) canonicalize trace.trace_id and trace.span_id fields from common vendor shapes (OTel, X-Request-Id, custom); 3) attach tenant_id and tenant_alias mapping using tenant-mapping table; 4) emit sanitized log body and a compact label set to Loki via the existing loki-ingest gateway; 5) produce an optional 'trace-anchor' event to a dedicated traces-log index for fast reverse-lookup. Performance target: <=2ms median added latency for hot-path HTTP logs at 1000 rps per instance.
out_of_scope: Full reingestion tooling, long-term retention, or changing upstream SDKs. Heavy-weight stateful correlation reassembly (we will rely on lighter-weight deterministic translation only).
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end test demonstrating a trace id from a synthetic request appears in trace view and the corresponding log lines in Loki within 5s. 2) Generated Loki label cardinality must not increase by more than 3% for the test tenant dataset. 3) Bridge CPU and memory should not exceed 50% of baseline at 1k rps per instance in our perf harness. 4) Unit and integration tests covering parsing of at least 6 common trace id shapes.
implementation_notes:
- Parser table for candidate trace fields: trace.trace_id, traceid, X-Amzn-Trace-Id, x-request-id, span_id. Normalize to 32-hex lowercase where possible.
- Tenant mapping via a read-only snapshot fetched from config-store; mapping includes tenant_id, alias, and privacy level.
- Emit loki labels: tenant_id, service, env, trace_id_short (first 8 chars) to limit cardinality; write full trace_id to message body for exact matching when necessary.
- Add per-tenant sampling hints header 'x-rw-trace-sample' propagated to downstream metrics.
- Keep transformation pipeline in a single small binary (Go) with pluggable parsers; avoid heavyweight regexes.
- Provide a compatibility shim for current loki-ingest endpoint (no schema change).
risks:
1) Label cardinality growth if services start tagging arbitrary IDs as labels. Mitigation: enforce label whitelist and automatic dropper.
2) Latency regression on hot paths if parsing is expensive. Mitigation: use fast-json parser and limit deep extraction.
3) Tenant mapping staleness leading to misattribution. Mitigation: refresh snapshots and emit metrics on mapping-misses.
4) False confidence: short trace_id label may cause collisions for debugging. Document trade-off and provide 'full-trace' toggle for on-demand mode.
rollback_plan: If Loki label cardinality spikes or ingestion errors increase, immediately disable bridge via feature flag and revert traffic to existing pipeline. We will have a canary rollout with 5% traffic initially and dashboards to watch for error rate, ingest throughput, and unique label count. Manual DNS/route rollback instructions are in the runbook.
qa_and_testing:
- Unit tests for parser permutations.
- Integration test using the perf harness: synthetic producer -> bridge -> loki-mock -> verify labels and body.
- End-to-end smoke: instrumented request in staging that generates trace and logs; confirm trace to log join in Grafana panel.
- Load test at 2x expected peak to validate tail latencies.
- Security scan of binary and container image; dependency upgrade policy applied.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged canary (5% traffic) for 48 hours with alerts on error rates and unique label counts. 2) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% over 5 days if thresholds stable. 3) Post-rollout evaluation window (7 days) to validate dashboards and SLO impact. 4) If issues, rollback via feature flag immediately.
